blind_allowed.cluster_live: OCI session expires every 1-2h and kubectl exec-auth fails from the Mac (crew#345); the same producers are graded from git under cluster/*

entries.reader: science/datamap.py collected() reads every facts row; science/dbt builds on it

entries.why: 76k session transcripts, 6.5 GB. Every tool call, every result, every word he typed. Only per-day spend is extracted. This is the largest unread asset the estate owns and the one that would answer most questions about how agents work.
1.2 GB of the CLI's own failed telemetry uploads. Not our data, not our schema, and it grows without bound. The correct action is deletion and a size guard, not ingestion.
2,330 scored candidate dossiers, 131 MB, stranded in an abandoned agent worktree. Every vetting decision the estate has ever made is in here and the live store beside it holds zero files.
28.5 MB, one file per tool decision. The `toolguard` source in the warehouse carries counters only, so which tool call was refused and why is not queryable.
One file per sensing cycle. What maestro noticed is recorded; whether it was right is not, because nothing joins an intent to what happened next.
The skills maestro can heal with. Read live by maestro, never sampled into a series, so 'is the experience graph growing' has no answer.
Job coordination state. Small, and the timeline files beside it are the part worth having.
6,932 of his prompts. Now collected in DERIVED form as the daily `attention` counts, which is a count of his messages and not the messages. The text itself is still unqueryable.
7,046 rows recording the same prompts as `directives`, in a second format, with an open/closed state the other one lacks. Two ledgers of one thing (LAW 39).
12,928 rows, the largest single-file ledger on the machine and the only one spanning every project. Nothing reads it.
11 local tickets that do not join to the 26 GitHub issues. The duplication is the finding; collecting it is how the duplication becomes visible.
Six per-job timeline files, 316 rows. No code refers to any of them, so these are the clearest deletion candidates on the machine.
The peer channel under `.estate`. A second copy of the board already collected from `~/.claude`, and no code refers to this one.
Push receipts. Superseded by the `bundle_push` source.
Worktree cleanup receipts, 2 rows.
One row. The mechanism was replaced by the prompt ledger.
The live dossier store, and it holds zero files. Listed so the emptiness is a row rather than an absence.
A second copy of the experience graph, under `.estate`.
2 rows in 5,548 mention revenue. Every efficiency number is a cost over nothing.

entries.what: what an agent chose, and what it rejected
entries.why: The transcripts hold the reasoning and nothing extracts it. The `decisions` source was built for this and its writer has been dead 55 hours.

entries.what: what was researched, and what changed because of it
entries.why: RESEARCH-LEDGER.jsonl has 8 entries, all hand-written by an agent that remembered, and 0 of 8 record the decision the research fed. LAW 35 has no mechanism.

entries.what: did the thing an agent built actually work
entries.why: Commits and PRs are counted. Whether the change held, was reverted, or broke something is not, so there is no denominator for quality.

entries.what: how long each scheduled job takes
entries.why: launchd runs 43 jobs and records exit codes in log files. No series of durations exists, so 'is anything getting slower' is unanswerable.

entries.what: what a guard refused, and whether the refusal was correct
entries.why: LAW 38 grades a guard by whether it allows correct work. Refusals are counted; false refusals are not recorded at all, so the law cannot be measured.

entries.what: which model served each call, and what it cost
entries.why: `spend` records dollars per owner per day. Cost per model, per task type and per outcome is in the transcripts and is not extracted.

entries.what: tokens spent re-reading context that did not change
entries.why: `method_metrics` computes output tokens per call for one project, once. It is a single row, generated by hand, not a series.
The job runs under launchd with no hc-wrap ping, so it can stop and nothing records that it did. run_duration and last_exit_status are never written anywhere.
Every refusal a guard makes vanishes when the hook exits; false refusals are not recorded, so LAW 38 cannot be measured. Same act as act/guard_outcome.
Listeners receive events and no ledger counts what arrived, what was dropped or when the last event came.
An archived checkout is kept for reading, not measured.

entries.reader: scripts/estate-snapshot delivery() (commits no remote holds, dirty files, oldest stranded commit) and gh search prs merged 7d

entries.why: One sqlite per Dagster run; the run index (index.db) is the store, the per-run files are its shards.
Dagster's own run and schedule history. Whether any scheduled asset ran, or how long, is answerable only inside Dagster's UI.
Temporal's dev-server history. Workflow durations and failures are in it and nothing extracts them.
The sovereign worker's spend ledger. Nothing joins it to spend_daily in the warehouse.
A checkout the snapshot job clones; the ledgers inside are copies of crew/science/*.jsonl, already collected from the live tree.
Board deliveries that failed. Four rows, never read, so a broken board delivery is invisible.
A shadow-mode guard's would-have-refused log. Reading it is the only way to know if the guard is safe to arm.
One row. The estate registry writer; nothing reads it back.
Founder requirements ledger, 5 rows, no reader.
24,953 capability receipts, 10 MB. The largest ledger under ~/.estate and no collector names it.
372 alerts delivered to the founder inbox; whether any was acted on is not recorded.
Sovereign worker receipts, 15 rows, no reader.
A manifest yaml.safe_load cannot parse is a producer whose shape nobody can read.

entries.reader: SigNoz OTLP (platform/observability/signoz.yaml) and Langfuse callback (platform/llm/config.yaml) receive every request as a trace

entries.why: Flux alerting is opt-in by a hand-typed namespace allowlist, so a failed reconcile outside it is silent (crew#344).
Same allowlist as HelmRelease: reconcile failures outside the alert namespaces reach nobody (crew#344).
Source fetch failures are Flux conditions nothing exports (crew#344).

entries.reader: Flux notification-controller Provider (the alert IS the reader for the namespaces it names)

entries.why: A namespace has no series of its own; its pods are graded under their Deployments.
Declarative config; its revisions are git history, already held.
Declarative; whether it matched is graded under Kyverno admission, which is a cluster_live measure.
Sync failures are a condition on the object; nothing scrapes or alerts on it, so a rotated upstream secret fails silently.
No kube-state-metrics, no ServiceMonitor, no PodMonitor in any manifest (recon 2026-08-26). Restarts, replicas ready, request rates and PVC usage exist in the API server and nothing reads them.
The running cluster is the same producers as cluster/*, read live; graded under the same ticket.
Five public hostnames and no uptime probe, TLS-expiry check or latency series anywhere in the estate; langfuse.mumchimp.com was down 2+ days unnoticed (crew#340).
34 hook commands run on every session start, prompt, tool use and stop; none records its verdict, so refusal rate and latency are unmeasurable. Same act as act/guard_outcome.
Three MCP servers answer tool calls from every session and no ledger records a call, an error or a latency.

entries.reader: scripts/estate-snapshot delivery() via gh search prs merged 7d; per-repo issue and PR age are not read

entries.why: Workflow runs have durations, queue waits and pass rates in the Actions API; nothing pulls them, so 'is CI getting slower' is unanswerable. Same act as act/run_duration.
Session transcripts per project. Only per-day spend is extracted; tool calls, failures and founder messages are unread (crew#319).
